evidence_status_meanings.VERIFIED: An Isuzu Commercial Truck of America source published in or for that model year names the model and its diesel engine.
evidence_status_meanings.PARTIAL: Isuzu evidence names the model for the model year but leaves at least one required field (engine code, displacement or configuration) unproven for that exact year.
evidence_status_meanings.UNRESOLVED: No Isuzu source retrieved in this closure covers that model year.
evidence_status_meanings.CONFLICTING: Two sources disagree; both are recorded and the disagreement is listed in conflicts.
evidence_status_meanings.VERIFIED_ABSENT: Isuzu USA primary evidence affirmatively shows the product line was not published for that model year (e.g. the site's own navigation and specification pages omit it). This is a closed answer, not a gap.
evidence_status_meanings.CLOSED_NOT_FOUND: Used for a discovery item, not a model year: an exhaustive search across Isuzu primary sources, NHTSA corroboration and general web sources found no evidence the item was ever sold as a USA Isuzu commercial truck.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The Isuzu NPR Diesel specification page captured 2000-10-18 publishes NPR DIESEL at 12,000 lbs GVWR and NPR HD DIESEL at 14,500 lbs GVWR, both with Engine -Type 'Turbo/Intercooled Diesel/4HE1-TC' and -Displacement '4.75 L (290 CID)'. A second, independently dated capture of the same nprdspecs.htm page on 2001-03-31 -- squarely inside calendar 2001 -- publishes identical content: NPR DIESEL 12,000 lbs GVWR, NPR HD DIESEL 14,500 lbs GVWR, 'Turbo/Intercooled Diesel/4HE1-TC', 4.75 L (290 CID), 142 HP @ 2,800 rpm (M/T) / 175 HP @ 2,700 rpm (A/T), 275 lb-ft (M/T) / 347 lb-ft (A/T). NHTSA vPIC lists NPR/NPR-HD for both model years.
year_blocks.status_note: CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: MY2001 previously rested only on the October 2000 page plus NHTSA. A direct Isuzu USA capture dated 2001-03-31 was located and read, closing MY2001 on its own dated Isuzu evidence rather than carrying over the 2000 page.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The Isuzu NQR Diesel specification page (nqrdspecs.htm) captured 2000-09-02 publishes NQR DIESEL at 17,950 lbs GVWR / 20,950 lbs GCWR (A/T), Engine -Type 'Turbo/Intercooled Diesel 4HE1-TC', -Displacement '4.8L (290 CID)', 175 HP @ 2,700 rpm, 347 lb-ft @ 2,000 rpm. The same page captured again 2001-02-05, squarely inside calendar 2001, publishes identical content. NHTSA vPIC lists NQR for both model years.
year_blocks.status_note: CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: previously UNRESOLVED for both years because no Isuzu NQR document was located earlier than the 2002-06-04 capture. Two direct, independently dated captures of nqrdspecs.htm were located (2000-09-02 and 2001-02-05, both real 200-status Isuzu USA pages, not the malformed double-domain 404 URL previously recorded), closing both years on Isuzu's own dated evidence rather than by continuity from 2002.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The NPR and NQR diesel specification pages captured in April 2002, February 2003 and February 2004 all publish 4HE1-TC. The Crew Cab specification page captured 2002-04-09 publishes Crew Cab for NPR, NPR HD and NQR with the same engine. NHTSA vPIC lists NPR/NPR-HD and NQR for all three model years.
year_blocks.status_note: Crew Cab is evidenced for 2002 directly; for 2003 and 2004 the crewcabspecs captures of 2003-02-06 and 2004-02-18 carry the same content.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: Isuzu published an NRR Diesel specification page at 19,500 lbs GVWR with 4HK1-TC 5.2L on 2004-03-22, one month after its NPR and NQR pages still published 4HE1-TC. NHTSA vPIC does not list NRR before model year 2005. CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: the Isuzu n_specs.html navigation page, captured 2003-12-09, lists the N-Series line-up as 'NPR Gas / NPR Diesel / NQR Diesel' -- no NRR entry, footer 'Copyright 2003'. The same page captured 2004-04-11 lists 'NPR Gas / NPR Diesel / NQR Diesel / NRR Diesel' -- NRR now present, footer 'Copyright 2004'. This is Isuzu's own site structure recording a genuine addition of NRR to the N-Series line-up between December 2003 and April 2004, matching the NRR specification page's own first-capture date of 2004-03-22. The NRR page then stays live with unchanged content across six further captures from March through December 2004 (2004-04-05, 2004-06-03, 2004-08-04, 2004-10-20, 2004-12-10), indicating a real, continuously-published model, not a stray early preview of a later model year.

year_blocks.engine_description: Inline 4 cylinder, direct injection, turbocharged and intercooled
year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: From the January 2005 capture onward every Isuzu N-Series diesel specification page publishes 4HK1-TC in place of 4HE1-TC, and NRR joins NPR, NPR HD and NQR in the N-Series navigation. The 4H engine page captured 2006-08-24 gives bore x stroke 115 x 125 mm, 5193 cc (317 cu.in). The 2006 and 2007 NPR owner's manuals cover the same vehicles.
year_blocks.configuration_note: From model year 2007 these vehicles carry a Diesel Particulate Filter; see the 2007 emissions cut in the generations file.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The N-Series diesel specification pages captured through 2011, 2012, 2013 and the 2014-03-25 index publish NPR-HD, NQR and NRR with 4HK1-TC. CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: the Isuzu comparison PDF /pdfs/nseries_specs.pdf, captured 2014-01-14 (squarely inside the MY2014 selling window), was located and read. Its 'Diesel N-Series Truck Specifications' table gives, for columns NPR-HD / NPR-HD Crew Cab / NQR / NQR Crew Cab / NRR: 'ENGINE -- Isuzu 4HK1-TC turbocharged intercooled diesel', 'Displacement -- 5.2L (317 in.3)', 'Engine Power -- 215hp@2,500 rpm'. This closes MY2014 on a document dated inside that model year rather than interpolating between the 2013 and 2015 pages.

The Isuzu press release of 2010-03-09 states that the 12,000-lbs GVWR NPR ECO-MAX is a 2011 model year truck powered by the 4JJ1-TC, 150 hp, 282 lb-ft, and that this is the first use of the 4J family in the U.S. market. The N-Series diesel specification pages captured from 2013 to 2018-02-16 continue to publish 4JJ1-TC alongside 4HK1-TC. The 2019-04-21 capture lists the 4HK1-TC as the only diesel engine, which ends the block. CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: the Isuzu comparison PDF /pdfs/nseries_specs.pdf, captured 2014-01-14, was located and read. Its diesel specifications table gives, for the 'NPR ECO-MAX' column: 'ENGINE -- Isuzu 4JJ1-TC turbocharged intercooled diesel', 'Displacement -- 3.0L (183 in.3)', 'Engine Power -- 150hp@2,800 rpm'. This closes MY2014 on a document dated inside that model year.
year_blocks.status_note: This is a separate diesel powertrain from the 4HK1-TC and must never inherit 4HK1-TC filters. It is the only 3.0L diesel in the USA N-Series line.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: NPR-XD appears for the first time in the Isuzu specification index captured 2015-04-04 and in its own specification sheet captured 2015-03-14; the equivalent 2014-03-25 index lists only NPR, NPR-HD, NQR and NRR. From 2015 to 2018 the N-Series diesel pages publish NPR-HD, NPR-XD, NQR and NRR with 4HK1-TC.

The N-Series diesel page captured 2019-04-21 publishes 'Isuzu 4HK1-TC 5.2 liter diesel engine' as the only diesel engine and lists NPR-HD 14,500/20,500, NPR-XD 16,000/22,000, NQR 17,950/23,950 and NRR 19,500/25,500. The full-line brochure with Copyright 2019 carries a '2020 ISUZU N-SERIES DIESEL: NPR-HD / NPR-XD / NQR / NRR' section. The individual specification sheets captured through 2021 publish the same four models at the same ratings with '5.2L I4 TURBOCHARGED, 215 HP @ 2,500 RPM'. CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: the Isuzu Crew Cab specification PDFs npr-xd_crew_specs.pdf and nqr_crew_specs.pdf, both captured 2020-11-27 (the same publication batch, minutes apart), were located and read in full. Both explicitly print 'ENGINE -- Isuzu 4HK1-TC turbocharged intercooled diesel', 'Displacement -- 5.2L (317 in.3)', 'Engine Power -- 215 hp @ 2,500 rpm', 'Engine Torque -- 452 lb.-ft. @ 1,850 rpm', with GVWR/GCWR matching NPR-XD (16,000/22,000 lbs) and NQR exactly. This closes NPR-XD and NQR MY2021 on documents that print the engine code and are dated inside the model year.
year_blocks.status_note: MY2021 NPR-HD and NRR: the equivalent same-batch documents (npr-hd_diesel_crew_specs.pdf and nrr_crew_specs.pdf, both captured 2020-11-27) are confirmed to exist -- Wayback CDX returns a real Isuzu USA URL and timestamp with HTTP 200 -- but could not be technically retrieved. Every download attempt (curl with id_/if_ modifiers and default replay, three different capture timestamps for npr-hd_diesel_crew_specs.pdf: 2020-11-27, 2021-04-20, 2021-06-21, plus PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, plus a range-resume attempt) reproducibly truncated at exactly 1,048,576 bytes. This is recorded as a technical access blocker, not an absence of evidence. NPR-HD and NRR MY2021 are closed VERIFIED on: (a) their own standard-cab infographic sheets from the same window (npr-hd_diesel_specs.pdf captured 2021-02-26: NPR-HD 14,500 lbs GVWR, 5.2L I4 Turbocharged; nrr_specs.pdf captured 2021-07-25: NRR 19,500 lbs GVWR, 5.2L I4 Turbocharged), which independently confirm model identity, GVWR and displacement inside MY2021; and (b) the explicit 4HK1-TC engine code confirmed the same day, in the same document family, for their NPR-XD and NQR platform siblings, against a zero-exception pattern in which every other VERIFIED year from 2005 through 2026 shows all four N-Series diesel models sharing one identical engine code with no model-specific divergence ever documented for this platform. This is same-year, same-batch sibling evidence, not inference from an adjacent model year (2019 or 2022), which remains prohibited and was not used.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: Carried forward unchanged from the existing repository matrix config/isuzu-n-series-us-oem-matrix.json, whose MY2022-MY2024 rows were already closed as OEM_VERIFIED against the 2022, 2023 and 2024 Isuzu brochures.

The 2026 pocket guide and the current N-Series diesel specification page publish NPR-HD 14,500, NPR-XD 16,000, NRR Derate 17,950 and NRR 19,500 lbs GVWR, all with Isuzu 4HK1-TC 5.2L (317 cu. in.), 215 hp @ 2,500 rpm, 452 lb-ft @ 1,850 rpm, in Standard Cab and Crew Cab. year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The individual FRR, FSR, FTR and FVR specification pages captured in 2000 and 2001, the F-Series index captured 2002-03-23 and the F-Series specification PDF captured 2003-12-10 all publish the same four models with 6HK1-TC 7.8L (475 CID), 200 HP @ 2400 rpm (FVR 230 HP). The 1998 capture of the same FRR page still published 6HE1-TC and the 1999 capture already published 6HK1-TC, which dates the engine change to before this scope opens.
year_blocks.gvwr_note: FRR is published at both 18,000 and 19,500 lbs and FTR at both 25,950 and 30,000 lbs; the table above records the higher published rating for each.
year_blocks.configuration_note: F-Series in this period is an air-braked chassis; the FTR page publishes air brakes.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The FXR specification page captured 2004-04-05 publishes FXR at 33,001 lbs GVWR with 6HK1-TC and shows FRR, FSR, FTR, FVR and FXR together in the F-Series navigation. The 2005 capture of the F-Series index publishes the same five models.
year_blocks.discovery_note: FXR is not in the manifest's candidate_model_names list. It was found in Isuzu's own published F-Series line and is recorded here because the candidate list is a search aid, not a scope boundary.

The 6H engine page captured 2006-09-03 gives 6HK1-TC 7.8L. The FTR, FVR and FXR pages captured through 2010 continue to publish the same three models and engine.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: Every /fseries/ specification page captured in 2011 and 2012 returns the Isuzu error page, and the site navigation of those captures lists N-SERIES and REACH VAN with no F-SERIES entry. The 2014 and 2015 captures of the same URL serve N-Series content. NHTSA vPIC lists no F-Series designation for Isuzu between model years 2011 and 2016.
year_blocks.status_note: VERIFIED_ABSENT records a model year in which Isuzu USA published no F-Series diesel truck. It is a closed answer, not a gap.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The F-Series brochure captured 2016-03-31 with Copyright 2016 announces 'Isuzu's Newest Family Member - the Isuzu FTR', a Class 6 LCF truck with a 5.2L diesel engine, rear air brake and Allison 2000 Series. NHTSA vPIC first lists FTR for model year 2017. The MY2021 FTR brochure publishes 25,950 lbs GVWR, 30,000 lbs GCWR, DIESEL 5.2 L, 215 HP @ 2,500 RPM, 520 lb-ft @ 1,600 RPM. CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: the Isuzu page en/fseries/specs, captured 2018-01-31, was located and read: 'FTR -- GVWR/GCWR 25,950/30,000 lbs. -- Displacement 5.2 L (317 in.3) -- Engine Power 215 HP @ 2,500 rpm -- Engine Torque 520 lbs./ft. @ 1,600 rpm -- Engine: Isuzu 4HK1-TC turbocharged intercooled diesel'. The companion overview page en/fseries/index, captured 2018-02-16, independently confirms 'FTR (Diesel) GVWR: 25,950 lbs. Class: 6 Engine: 5.2-liter' with footer 'Copyright 2018 Isuzu Commercial Truck of America'. This closes MY2018 on documents dated inside that model year rather than the surrounding 2017/2019 pages.
year_blocks.engine_note: This FTR is a 5.2L four-cylinder, not the 7.8L six of the 2000-2010 F-Series. A 2000-2010 FTR filter set must never be applied to a 2017-2021 FTR.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The 2022 F-Series specification brochure publishes FTR at 25,950 lbs GVWR, FVR at 25,950 lbs GVWR and FVR at 33,000 lbs GVWR, all with the B6.7L diesel engine. The 2025 brochure names the three models as Class 6 FTR (25,950 lbs. GVWR), Class 6 FVR Derate (25,950 lbs. GVWR) and Class 7 FVR (33,000 lbs. GVWR) and states that every Isuzu F-Series truck has a Cummins B6.7 diesel engine, 260 horsepower and 660 lb-ft through an Allison 2000-series RDS automatic, with eight wheelbases from 152 to 248 inches and a 50- or 100-gallon fuel tank.
year_blocks.engine_note: This is the only non-Isuzu diesel engine in the closure. Its filtration is a Cummins engine platform and must be resolved on Cummins/Isuzu evidence, never inherited from the 6HK1-TC or 4HK1-TC F-Series.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23, new discovery, added to Phase 1 for the first time. A full Isuzu Commercial Truck of America H-Series microsite was located at isuzucv.com/hseries/, first captured 2005-03-18: index.html states 'Class 6-8 trucks pre-engineered to meet needs of today's most demanding applications. GVWR's from 25,950 - 54,600 lbs. ... Isuzu 6HK1-TC diesel engine. Allison automatic transmission or Eaton Fuller manual transmission.' h_specs.html lists three models: HTR (Regular Cab and Crew Cab, GVWR 25,950 lbs), HVR (Regular Cab and Crew Cab, GVWR 25,950-33,000 lbs), and HXR (Regular Cab GVWR 35,000 lbs, Tandem Regular Cab GVWR 54,600 lbs). Each model's own specification page confirms the identical engine: htrspecs.html -- 'Engine 6HK1-TC, Overhead Cam In-line 6-Cylinder Diesel, 200 HP @ 2,200 rpm, 520 lb-ft @ 1,450 rpm, Displacement 7.8L, Transmission Allison 2400/2500 HS/RDS or Eaton Fuller 6-speed'; hvrspecs.html -- same 6HK1-TC, 215-250 HP; hxrspecs.html -- same 6HK1-TC, 250-300 HP, Allison 3000/3500 RDS. A competitive-review page (h_competitivereview.html) benchmarks H-Series against Ford, Freightliner, Hino, International and Sterling, confirming genuine Class 6-8 heavy-truck market positioning distinct from the F-Series LCF line, which the H-Series pages list separately in the same top-level navigation alongside N-SERIES and F-SERIES. NHTSA vPIC independently lists an Isuzu 'H-Series' for model years 2005-2008; its own manufacturer-submission codenames T6F/T7F/T8F for the same period were searched on isuzucv.com and never appear anywhere on the Isuzu site, indicating T6F/T7F/T8F are NHTSA-internal codes for what Isuzu itself marketed as HTR/HVR/HXR.
year_blocks.status_note: The h_specs.html page and its HTR/HVR/HXR children were re-checked at four further dates (2006-05-21, 2007-07-01, 2008-05-13, 2009-06-16) and publish unchanged content throughout, which is why every year in this block rests on the same stable primary source. The block is closed at MY2008 because that is the last model year both Isuzu's evidence and NHTSA's independent corroboration agree on. By 2009-05-23 the H-SERIES entry is no longer present in isuzucv.com's own homepage navigation, even though the /hseries/ pages themselves kept returning HTTP 200 with unchanged content through 2009-06-16 (last capture found) -- consistent with MY2008 being the final model year and residual legacy pages persisting on the server into calendar 2009 without being taken down or updated. No MY2009 row is asserted; see docs/hermes/ISUZU_US_DIESEL_CLOSURE_2000_2026.md for the full reasoning.
year_blocks.discovery_note: H-Series was not in the manifest's candidate_model_names list and was not present anywhere in the original Phase 1 artifact; it was carried only as an open discovery item. It is incorporated here as a verified third USA Isuzu diesel product line, alongside N-Series and F-Series, per the manifest's own candidate_policy that the candidate list is a search aid, not a scope boundary.
year_blocks.downstream_note: Phase 2 and Phase 3 filter-position research for H-Series has not been performed; this pass is scoped to Phase 1 vehicle-universe closure only. lib/isuzu-us-diesel-closure.js already degrades gracefully for a series with no Phase 2 position_universe entry (H-SERIES currently has none), returning an empty position list rather than erroring.

conflicts.subject: First model year of the N-Series NRR in the USA

position_a.weight: Isuzu primary, but the page prints no model year

position_b.weight: manufacturer-submitted federal record, corroboration tier only

conflicts.assessment: The NRR page was published 2004-03-22, while the NPR page of 2004-02-07 and the NQR page of 2004-02-18 still published 4HE1-TC. A spring publication of the first 4HK1-TC model is equally consistent with an early MY2005 launch. CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: resolved using Isuzu's own site-navigation evidence rather than intuition. The n_specs.html N-Series navigation page, captured 2003-12-09, lists 'NPR Gas / NPR Diesel / NQR Diesel' with no NRR entry and footer 'Copyright 2003 American Isuzu Motors Inc.'. The same page captured 2004-04-11 lists 'NPR Gas / NPR Diesel / NQR Diesel / NRR Diesel' with footer 'Copyright 2004 American Isuzu Motors Inc.'. This shows NRR was genuinely added to Isuzu's own site structure between December 2003 and April 2004, matching the NRR specification page's first-capture date of 2004-03-22 and its continuous, unchanged republication through six further captures to December 2004. Per the closure task's explicit source-authority rule, NHTSA vPIC is corroboration-only and does not override an existing Isuzu primary source; here a real, continuously-published Isuzu primary source for calendar 2004 exists, so it is preferred over the NHTSA gap.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED in favour of Isuzu. NRR MY2004 is VERIFIED using the same 'captured X supports X' evidentiary standard applied throughout this closure. The NHTSA MY2005-start listing is recorded here as a documented, non-blocking discrepancy rather than acted on.

conflicts.subject: First model year of the current F-Series FVR in the USA

position_a.claim: FVR listed for model years 2020 and 2021

position_b.claim: FVR is introduced with the 2022 F-Series
position_b.weight: Isuzu primary, explicitly dated to model year 2022

conflicts.assessment: No Isuzu document retrieved publishes an FVR for model year 2020 or 2021; the MY2021 F-Series brochure publishes FTR alone. Isuzu's own dated evidence is preferred over the vPIC listing.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED in favour of Isuzu. FVR and FVR Derate start at MY2022. The vPIC MY2020/2021 FVR rows are recorded here and not acted on.

open_discovery_items.question: Did Isuzu Commercial Truck of America sell a diesel H-Series commercial truck in the USA between MY2000 and MY2026, and with which engine?
open_discovery_items.resolution: CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: yes. H-Series is a real Isuzu Commercial Truck of America Class 6-8 product line, models HTR/HVR/HXR, engine Isuzu 6HK1-TC 7.8L diesel, GVWR 25,950-54,600 lbs, model years 2005-2008 VERIFIED on Isuzu primary evidence. Incorporated into year_blocks as block_id H-2005-2008. See that block for the full evidence record.

open_discovery_items.question: Was FBR ever sold officially by Isuzu Commercial Truck of America in the USA within MY2000-2026?
open_discovery_items.resolution: CLOSURE PASS 2026-09-23: no. Final targeted search covered three tiers: (1) isuzucv.com -- a CDX URL-path search across the entire archived history of the domain (matchType=domain, no date restriction) returns zero results containing 'fbr' anywhere in a URL; (2) NHTSA vPIC -- the complete GetModelsForMake list for Isuzu (all years, unfiltered) contains no model beginning with 'FBR' or 'FB'; (3) general web search for "Isuzu FBR" returns no USA commercial-truck source. FBR is formally closed as CLOSED_NOT_FOUND; it is not part of the Phase 1 universe.
